sets.s: “Crossing the road here will be quicker than using the traffic lights, but remember to look right as that’s where the vehicles are coming from.”
i: The vehicles should be driving down the correct side of the road.
M
This assumption is made (and taken for granted), because you wouldn’t expect a car to be going down the road in the wrong direction.
It would be easier to cross the road here rather than using the traffic lights.
N
The statement only implies the journey will take less time, not that this means speeding up the process will be easier.
The group is trying to cross the road as quickly as possible.
M
It is assumed that they would be trying to cross the road as fast as possible, because they are looking into faster means of getting there.

sets.s: “Wearing a jacket will help to keep you warm, and the extra pockets will be of use, so it’s advisable to bring one.”
i: The person being spoken to will be doing something that requires the use of pockets.
M
The statement implies that having the extra pockets will be a helpful addition for what they are doing, so it is safe to assume the pockets will be needed.
The recipient of this statement has a jacket to bring.
N
The statement is a clear recommendation, not based on what the recipient can or cannot do.
At least a part of the activity that the jacket would be useful for will be in a cold environment.
M
The jacket is said to help keep you warm, this assumes that it will be cold at a point it and therefore justifies the precaution. Therefore, assumption made.

sets.s: “The former captain of the Spanish football team made a deal with her manager that she would play for another five more years, but ended up retiring after three, causing much anger amongst the fans.”
i: It was wrong of the football captain to quit before the five years was over.
N
The statement is only stating facts of what happened. We cannot assume this was the wrong decision to make.
Many of her fans wanted her to carry on as captain.
M
It is assumed that the fans wanted her to carry on, because when she quit there was a lot of anger – a negative reaction to it.
The manager at the time of the deal was still her manager when she quit.
N

The statement only talks about the manager when making the deal. It does not mention who the manager was when she quit or whether the manager had changed. This piece of information is not assumed in the passage.

sets.s: “You’d have better luck winning the race with lighter clothing and springier shoes. First place will guarantee you a spot in the final.”
i: The person receiving this information wants to avoid a spot in the final.
N
The statement gives advice on how to race better and get into the final. It is not assumed that the person wants to not be part of this.
Finishing in first place is the only way to get to the final.
N
The statement only says that finishing first can guarantee it, so it is not safe to assume there are no alternative ways to achieving this.
The recipient of this statement is able to wear lighter clothing and use springier shoes.
N
The statement is purely providing the recipient with information, so they then have the chance to take action – if they can.
